title: Enforce release freeze when error budget is exhausted (tier-aware)
author: Connor O'Brien
release_notes: CI/CD: Non-emergency deploys are blocked when a tier’s 30d error budget is exhausted; emergency override requires incident context and is fully audited.
description: Summary: This PR tightens the deploy gate introduced in pr-28510 (warn-only) by enforcing a release freeze when a tier’s error budget is exhausted. When the gate is in a BLOCK state, non-emergency deploys fail fast in CI and surface a clear remediation message (link to tier dashboard + runbook). Emergency deploys remain possible, but require an explicit override token and incident metadata, and are posted to #eng-sre for auditability. Motivation: We’ve had recurring cases where we continued shipping feature rollouts during active budget exhaustion, prolonging recovery and making ownership ambiguous. This change aligns enforcement with the approved error budget policy (multi-window burn alerts + consequences) and creates a consistent “stop the line” behavior per tier. Policy behavior: (1) Gate evaluates the 30d rolling error budget state for the target tier(s) impacted by the deploy (hosted_shared, dedicated_reserved). (2) If budget_remaining_percent <= 0.0 OR budget_state == EXHAUSTED, gate blocks by default. (3) Exceptions: emergency mitigation/rollback deployments only, with required override fields. (4) Overrides are logged (CI artifact + audit log event) and announced in Slack with a standard template. Emergency override procedure: To perform an emergency deploy when the tier budget is exhausted, set REDWOOD_DEPLOY_OVERRIDE=emergency and provide (a) INCIDENT_ID (PagerDuty/Slack/incidents thread permalink) and (b) REASON (1–2 sentences). The gate validates required fields, attaches them to the deploy metadata, and emits an audit event. If these fields are missing, the deploy is blocked. Implementation details: The gate uses the existing budget computation service endpoint (slo-budget-api) to fetch a tier-scoped status snapshot (window=30d, refresh_tolerance=10m). The gate is intentionally conservative: if the budget service is unreachable or returns stale data beyond tolerance, we fail closed for non-emergency deploys (and fail open only for rollbacks tagged as emergency). We also added unit tests around state transitions and a small integration test for the CI action wrapper. Operator UX: CI output includes (a) detected tier(s), (b) budget state, (c) link to the tiered SLO dashboard, (d) runbook link, and (e) instructions for emergency overrides. Rollout: This is enabled for Hosted and Dedicated pipelines in “enforced” mode. Sandbox/staging remains warn-only to reduce friction. Related: ENG-4941, error budget policy doc, and incident-bot burn summaries. Notes: We intentionally did not add per-model or per-customer gating here to avoid cardinality/ownership confusion; this gate is tier-scoped by design.

conversation: Aisha Bello (review): Can we confirm the definition of “exhausted” is strictly budget_remaining <= 0 on the canonical 30d window? We should avoid accidental blocks on short-term burn spikes (burn-rate alerts already cover that).

Connor O'Brien (author): Yes — this only blocks on the 30d budget snapshot reporting EXHAUSTED or remaining<=0. Burn alerts are separate and still page; we’re not blocking on burn-rate here to avoid flapping. Added an explicit comment + test case.
Jordan Lee (review): Fail-closed on budget API outage is good, but we need an emergency path that works even if the budget API is down (e.g., rollback during outage).

Connor O'Brien (author): Added “emergency + rollback” special-case: if override=emergency AND change_type=rollback, we allow deploy even when the budget API is unreachable, and we annotate the audit event with budget_state=UNKNOWN + reason.
Mina Haddad (review): How do we pick the tier(s) for a deploy? Routing changes can impact both hosted and dedicated depending on policy bundles.

Connor O'Brien (author): The gate reads impacted_tiers from the deploy manifest (generated during pipeline) and defaults to “hosted_shared” for gateway/routing bundles unless the manifest explicitly constrains scope. I added a note in docs and a safeguard: if impacted_tiers is empty, we block and ask for explicit scope (prevents accidental broad deploys).
Sahana Iyer (review): Please ensure overrides are not just Slack-only; we need durable audit logs for compliance and post-incident review.
Connor O'Brien (author): Done — override emits AUDIT_EVENT_DEPLOY_OVERRIDE with incident_id/reason/actor/pipeline + linked commit SHA. Slack is just a notification surface.
Rafael Mendes (review): Requesting a clearer runbook link and a standard message in CI so on-call isn’t debugging “why did my deploy fail?”.

Connor O'Brien (author): Updated CI output to include the error-budget breach mitigation runbook and the tiered SLO dashboard deep link. Added examples to docs/internal/deployments/error-budget-gate.md.
Aisha Bello (approval): Approved. This matches the enforcement phase expectations. Please coordinate enablement messaging in #eng-sre and with Release.
